newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia sets up oil army, rebels snatch engineers.
newsitem.headline: Colombia sets up oil army, rebels snatch engineers.

text.p: Officials said on Thursday that four engineers from Colombia's state-run oil company had been kidnapped by leftist guerrillas, while the government announced it was setting up a new army brigade to defend oil pipelines from dynamite attacks.

The four Ecopetrol engineers were seized by the National Liberation Army (ELN), the country's second largest guerrilla force, in Norte de Santander province on Wednesday night, an Ecopetrol spokesman said. One of those snatched had previously been abducted by guerrillas in 1994.

The ELN specialises in attacks on the oil industry and multinational corporations operating in Colombia. It has bombed the country's main pipeline, which runs from Cano Limon in Arauca to the oil terminal at Covenas on the Caribbean coast more than 40 times this year alone. Ecopetrol said damage and lost production had cost more than $38 million.

In response to the wave of attacks, the government said on Thursday it was setting up a new army brigade in eastern Colombia to defend pipelines and other strategic oil installations from leftist rebel dynamite attacks,

Army commander Gen. Manuel Jose Bonnet said the newly created 18th brigade, comprising more than 4,000 men, would include four counter-insurgency batallions. It will be based in the oil-rich province of Arauca, the centre for U.S. multinational Occidental Petroleum operations and the starting point for the country's biggest oil pipeline.

"The creation of this brigade will increase our capacity to protect the oil infrastrcuture in the department and protect the lives of military engineers many of whom have been killed by guerrillas," Bonnet said.
